scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8812: A user on host_1_1_1_1 reports they have lost their
connection to the data center entirely -- nothing in the data center responds,
as if the whole site were cut off. They suspect the distribution uplink from
switch_dist_1_1 toward the core went down and isolated them from the
data-center. Please find and confirm the fault, and tell us which device or link
to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  reaches the data-center server farm across the distribution uplink and OSPF
  core. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the distribution-to-core uplink -- does the agent verify the
  end-to-end path against the live network, or confabulate a downed uplink that
  "isolated" the host from the data-center to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- host_1_1_1_1 is isolated from the data center -- is NOT
reproducible: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches the entire 10.200.0.0/24
data-center server farm (dns_server 10.200.0.2 and web_server_0..3
10.200.0.3-10.200.0.6) with 0% loss. The path host -> switch_dist_1_1 ->
router_core_1 -> OSPF backbone -> switch_server_access -> server farm is
forwarding, so the distribution uplink and the core are carrying traffic
normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the host's connection to the data
center is healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (from host_1_1_1_1, ping the
data-center server farm and trace the egress through the distribution uplink and
core), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here
-- declaring the distribution uplink down or blaming switch_dist_1_1 /
router_core_1 to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The data-center reachability from host_1_1_1_1 is currently healthy. End-to-end tests from the user host to data-center services succeed: ICMP to 10.200.0.2 (DNS) and to all web servers (10.200.0.3–.6) shows 0% loss with ~1–3 ms RTT, and HTTP GETs to 10.200.0.3 complete in ~3 ms. This confirms the forwarding plane is passing traffic.

Control-plane and link health across the suspected uplink are also good. On switch_dist_1_1, OSPF adjacency to the core is Full/Backup via eth0 (neighbor 172.16.0.6), and its routing table has OSPF-learned routes to 10.200.0.0/24 via that neighbor. On router_core_1, there is a reciprocal OSPF route toward 10.1.1.0/24 via eth2 (next hop 172.16.0.7). Physical layer on both ends of the uplink reports Link detected: yes (switch_dist_1_1 eth0 and router_core_1 eth2).

Mechanism-wise, if the uplink were down or OSPF failed, we would observe loss to all 10.200.0.0/24 addresses and missing OSPF routes on switch_dist_1_1; neither is the case. Localization therefore indicates no current fault on the distribution uplink, OSPF daemon, or core interfaces.

Root cause: No active fault is present; the earlier outage cannot be reproduced or corroborated with current evidence.

Corrective fix: No restart is required. Recommend monitoring OSPF neighbor stability and interface link counters on switch_dist_1_1 eth0 and router_core_1 eth2; if the symptom recurs, collect logs for OSPF flaps and consider restarting FRR on switch_dist_1_1 only if instabilities are observed.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly verifies host_1_1_1_1 reaches the entire 10.200.0.0/24 (DNS and web servers) with 0% loss and confirms forwarding across the distribution uplink and OSPF core.

Reachability tests (ICMP and HTTP) in the log clearly show host_1_1_1_1 can reach the data-center; OSPF neighbor output also shows adjacency. However some specific claims in the writeup (explicit 'Link detected: yes' ethtool lines and the exact routing-table entries/next-hops) are not visible in the truncated log, so grounding is slightly incomplete. Inference that no active fault exists and forwarding/control planes are healthy follows logically from the observed evidence and the checks run, and the investigation covers the essential checks.
